title: Triaero Graro – chińska rama, polskie szutry i pół roku testowania

takeaways.text: After six months, including Spanish training and Polish gravel races of 100–200 km, it felt fast, stiff and road-like but not brutal with 45 mm tires; UCI-approved, with UDH, T47 and hidden rack/fender mounts.

ICAN approached the magazine and supplied the frame (Polish, automatic captions). In October 2026 the frame, fork, headset and seatpost cost just under PLN 3,200 (US$899) with free shipping, plus a large custom hand-paint catalogue.

ICAN rates 45 mm tires; the tester says about 49 mm fits and his 45 mm Tufos leave plenty of room. Earlier nominal 38–40 mm tires on wide rims felt too harsh on stony gravel, so he settled on 45 mm at about 25–28 psi.
His size S52 build (SRAM Rival/Force/Apex mix 1×12, aluminium FSA bar and stem, pedals, three cages, bag and mount) weighed 8.74 kg; he rides S52 at 169 cm with a zero-setback post.
The minimalist two-piece saddle clamp let the saddle shift over a hard bump until he paid closer attention to torque; integrated headset routing will mean more service work later.
Maximum 1× chainring is 42T (he runs 40T); a front-derailleur mount allows 2× builds.

disclosure: The reviewer says ICAN approached the magazine and supplied wheels, cockpit and the frame for testing; the build otherwise uses parts chosen by the reviewer.
summary: Polish magazine summary after six months of racing and 100–200 km gravel events on a size S52 Graro, covering sizing, 40 to 45 mm tire choices, the 8.74 kg as-ridden weight, mounts, UDH and one saddle-clamp slip.
